metaTitle: Sell Mineral Rights in Blanding, UT | San Juan County
metaDescription: Hold mineral rights near Blanding, Utah, close to Bears Ears and the Paradox Basin? We buy interests directly, with a written offer and no pressure to sign.
heroLead: Blanding sits between the Aneth Field to the south and the Cane Creek trend to the north, in a part of San Juan County shaped as much by uranium history as by oil and gas.
intro: Blanding has a layered mineral history — the surrounding Bears Ears region was a center of uranium and vanadium mining through the mid-twentieth century, and the same families who held mineral interests through that era often hold oil and gas rights on the same or adjacent tracts today. San Juan County's oil and gas activity ties into the broader Paradox Basin, and Blanding's central location means owners here can hold interests spanning a fairly wide geographic range within the county.

We buy mineral, royalty, and non-participating royalty interests near Blanding directly. If your family's deed references multiple mineral types from the uranium era, we will confirm exactly what still applies to any current oil and gas production before quoting.

sections.heading: Uranium-era deeds and what they mean for oil and gas today
paragraphs: Deeds from the uranium and vanadium boom era sometimes used broad 'all minerals' language, while others specifically reserved or conveyed uranium and vanadium separately from oil and gas. If your family's paperwork dates back to that period, we read it carefully to determine whether your oil and gas rights were affected by any later conveyance, since assuming continuity without checking is how ownership gets misstated.

sections.heading: A central point in a wide county
paragraphs: San Juan County is geographically large, and Blanding sits roughly in the middle of it, which means two families both listing a Blanding mailing address might hold minerals in very different parts of the Paradox Basin — one closer to Aneth's carbonate production, another closer to the Cane Creek shale near Moab. We always confirm the actual township, range, and section for your interest before discussing value.

faqs.question: My family's deed is from the uranium mining era. Does that affect our oil and gas rights?
faqs.answer: It can, depending on the exact language. We review the deed's reservation and conveyance terms as part of our title confirmation.

faqs.question: Is my Blanding-area interest tied to Aneth or to the Cane Creek trend near Moab?
faqs.answer: It depends on the exact legal description. We confirm the specific location before making an offer, since Blanding sits between both areas.

faqs.question: How do I find out which minerals my family actually still owns?
faqs.answer: Send us whatever deeds or division orders you have and we will trace the chain of title at the San Juan County Recorder's office.
